purpose: Source-backed general guidance; never evidence about a store SKU or an answer template.

principles: A label naming sensitive skin can support that intended target only; it does not prove irritation-free, symptom relief, fragrance-free or universal suitability.
Tear-free is about eyes; it does not establish suitability for sensitive skin. Do not transfer one label property to a different body area or outcome.
Avoid ingredients the customer knows they react to. Plant extracts, essential oils and unscented labels are not guarantees against reactions.
Testing a new cosmetic on a small skin area before general use is useful; stop using it if a reaction develops. Do not invent a test duration or leave-on time.
Do not call all parabens or all preservatives harmful or irritants for everyone. An individual allergy and a blanket ingredient ban are different claims.
General cleaning advice cannot certify an unspecified cleaner as safe for pets. Follow the actual product label for dilution, contact time, rinsing and re-entry.
Keep pets away during cleaning and until the treated area is dry as directed; keep cleaners away from their food and water. Drying alone does not establish safety for every chemical.
A floral, natural or essential-oil name does not prove pet safety. Do not mix unknown cleaners or add homemade chemicals.
